items.eu-dora::governance: Put ICT risk inside the same governance and control framework that oversees every other risk the organisation takes, with the management body ultimately accountable. DORA's Article 5 sets that tone from the top for financial entities operating in the EU.
items.eu-dora::ict-risk-framework: Maintain a documented ICT risk management framework covering the full life cycle: identifying, protecting against, detecting, responding to and recovering from ICT incidents, plus lessons-learned processes. DORA's Articles 6 and 8-14 lay out that lifecycle for EU financial entities.
items.eu-dora::incident-reporting: Classify ICT-related incidents, and report the major ones to the competent authority through a single streamlined channel within the regulation's timelines. DORA's Articles 17-19 require an incident-management process and reporting of major ICT-related incidents.
items.eu-dora::resilience-testing: Run a programme of digital operational resilience testing - vulnerability assessments, gap analyses and like-for-like tests - at a frequency proportionate to risk, and have critical systems tested at least yearly by independent parties. DORA's Articles 24-26 set out that testing regime for EU financial entities.
items.eu-dora::third-party-ict: Manage ICT third-party risk as part of the ICT risk framework, keep a register of all contractual arrangements for ICT services, and apply the regulation's required contractual provisions when using ICT providers - including those that supply AI services. DORA's Articles 28-30 set out that regime for EU financial entities.
items.eu-dora::incident-reporting-centralisati: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, assess whether reporting of major ICT-related incidents can be centralised through a single EU Hub and report on that feasibility to the EU institutions by 17 January 2025. DORA's Article 21 is a duty on the authorities, not on financial entities; it is carried here so the regime's reporting architecture stays visible without implying an entity obligation.
items.eu-dora::critical-provider-oversight: Expect EU-level oversight of ICT providers designated as critical: the ESAs designate critical ICT third-party service providers against set criteria, appoint a Lead Overseer, and run structured oversight through an Oversight Forum and a Joint Oversight Network. DORA's Articles 31-34 set out that oversight framework for providers serving EU financial entities, including providers of AI services.
items.eu-dora::resilience-testing-programme: In DORA's resilience-testing chapter, financial entities may only use TLPT testers of the highest suitability and reputability - technically and organisationally capable, certified or bound by formal codes of conduct, independently assured and insured - whether external or, with approval and conflict-of-interest safeguards, internal. Article 27's conditions attach to threat-led penetration testing of the live network, which can include AI-supported systems in scope.
items.eu-dora::cyber-threat-information-sharin: Financial entities may exchange cyber threat information and intelligence - indicators of compromise, tactics, techniques and procedures, alerts - with each other under DORA's Article 45, provided sharing happens within trusted communities and through arrangements that protect business confidentiality, personal data and competition rules. The article is permissive: it opens a lawful sharing route for AI operators rather than imposing an obligation.
